note: Seeded 2026-08-19 from the review record of 2026-07-24 to 2026-08-19. Occurrences are things that actually happened and cost time, each traceable to a dated review document in the agstack workplan. Nothing speculative is recorded here: a lesson with no incident behind it becomes noise, and noise is what discredits the checks that were earned.

lessons.trigger: A check, test or assertion reports success.
lessons.directive: Establish that it can fail. Show it failing on purpose, or show the count it produces changing when the underlying thing changes. A gate that cannot distinguish good from bad is worse than no gate, because it is believed.

occurrences.what: Tier 1 privacy was satisfied only vacuously: no holder_account could leak because no identity was ever produced.
The Tier 1 privacy test passed vacuously while Tier 1 still emitted the field.
The Tier 1 assertion could pass in isolation regardless of behaviour.
A cross-layer test was skipped in Pancake CI and the suite still reported green.
The schema drift guard passed while comparing nothing, because the mirror it compared against had been made permissive.
The dirty-tree warning fired on every single run because generated credentials were rewritten each time, so it stopped carrying information.
The lint ratchet counted ruff's success banner as a violation, so it reported 1 whatever the code said, and a real count of 36 rode in unnoticed across four commits.

lessons.trigger: One fact is represented in two places -- a mirror and the system it mirrors, a function and its caller, the same logic in two packages, a value in two config files.
lessons.directive: Change both in the same commit, and add a test that fails when they disagree. Do not rely on remembering the second one, because the second one is what gets forgotten.

occurrences.what: get_boundary_coverage was correct and had been called from nowhere since AR 1.0.
v2 GeoID minting was fully implemented and no service path called it.
GeoIDRegimeAlias rows were written by the migration and never read by the equivalence-set query.
The point-handling path existed in app/geoid_v2.py and was absent from migration/geoid_v2.py, so every pin was quarantined.
The phone constraint was relaxed in the migration mirror and not in the hub it mirrors, so the import reported 0 rejections where the real system would have rejected 85.
ruff was pinned in ci.yml and left unpinned in stomata.yml, so the gating workflow measured a different thing to the advisory one.

lessons.trigger: You are naming or counting what a run did, in a report, a log line, a status field or a document.
lessons.directive: Make the word mean one outcome. If a category can contain both a success and a failure, split it. Assert that the categories sum to the total and do not overlap, because every individual number can be computed correctly and the totals still describe a run that did not happen.

occurrences.what: TRACEABILITY.md documented Tiers 2 and 4 as implemented when they were not.
268 duplicate submissions that were correctly aliased to existing GeoIDs were reported as quarantined and as decisions required. Nothing had failed.
18,184 geometries were reported as altered by canonicalisation; the real figure was 3,597, the rest being points on a different code path that set the flag as a side effect.
The point count, the single most consequential fact about the run, did not appear in the report at all.
resolved_child_of was presented as a peer of imported_new when it is a subset, so 74 fields summed to 75 and read as one field processed twice.

lessons.trigger: You are about to quote a number, or cite a run, screenshot or log as evidence.
lessons.directive: Open the artifact and find the number in it. Cite the run that produced it, at the commit under review. A figure that cannot be located in the evidence is a recollection, and recollections drift toward what we hoped.

occurrences.what: Screenshots showed 2 fieldlists as though that were the corpus; it was an artifact of a --limit flag on the run.
A packet cited packets/evidence/schema1.log, which did not exist, and bias_curve.csv, which was at the repository root.
'The missing 13,343' was stated in prose and appeared nowhere in the run it described.
A summary quoted a pre-fix reconciliation of 13,658 + 14,594 + 30 while the attached log showed 27,978 + 275 + 29.

lessons.trigger: A guard, assertion or lint rule stands between you and a change you believe is correct.
lessons.directive: Change the claim or change the code, never quietly narrow the guard. If the guard is genuinely stale, say so in the commit message and re-record the baseline, so that weakening it costs a sentence someone can read.

occurrences.what: ruff.toml's ignore list was suppressing rule families including B008, so the linter was configured not to see real defects.
The phone column was removed from the drift guard's NOT NULL and UNIQUE lists so a change would pass, and the guard then certified an import that could not work.

lessons.trigger: You have identified a failure mode and are about to write it down in a document, review comment or email.
lessons.directive: Write the check as well, in the same change, or record explicitly that it cannot be mechanized and why. A paragraph is read once by whoever was in the conversation and then archived; it does not bind the person who arrives next, and it does not bind its own author a week later.

occurrences.what: Threshold guidance was written as prose reasoning; it rested on an IoU implementation that turned out to be wrong, and the prose gave no way to notice.
A document asked, in words, that checks not be waived silently. Five days later a guard was edited to pass and nothing objected.
The same document predicted that a check which becomes noise 'gets waived, then gets deleted'. Two checks became noise and were ignored for days by the author who wrote that sentence.

lessons.trigger: You are reading a run record, CI result or packet to decide whether a branch is sound.
lessons.directive: Check the commit the run was taken at against the tip being reviewed. Commits after the last recorded run are ungated, and that is exactly where an unnoticed regression sits.
lessons.advisory_because: One occurrence so far, and the commit-binding check already records the commit for a reader to compare. Promoting on a single incident manufactures the kind of speculative check that turns into noise. Revisit on the next occurrence.

occurrences.what: Run records sat at b3c55ed and ac6e536 while the branch tip was 17d3aaf, and a lint regression rode in on the four ungated commits between.
